notes.text: Behold — The prophet having given one eminent instance of God's certain fore-knowledge, in the deliverance of the Jews by Cyrus, now adds another more eminent example of it, by foretelling the coming of the Messiah. This place therefore is expressly interpreted of Christ, Matt. xii, 18, &c. And to him, and to him only, all the particulars following, truly and evidently belong. Whom - Whom I will enable to do and suffer all those things which belong to his office. Elect - Chosen by me to this great work. Delighteth - Both for himself and for all his people, being fully satisfied with that sacrifice, which he shall offer up to me. Bring forth - Shall publish or shew, as this word is translated, Matt. xii, 18. Judgment - The law, and will, and counsel of God, concerning man's salvation. Gentiles - Not only to the Jews, but to the Heathen nations.
Cry — In a way of contention, or ostentation. Lift - His voice. Heard - As contentious and vain-glorious persons frequently do.

Break — Christ will not deal rigorously with those that come to him, but he will use all gentleness, cherishing the smallest beginnings of grace, comforting and healing wounded consciences. Quench - That wick of a candle which is almost extinct, he will not quench, but revive and kindle it again. Judgment - The law of God, or the doctrine of the gospel, which he will bring forth, unto, with, or according to truth, that is, truly and faithfully.
'Till — 'Till he has established his law or doctrine, among the nations of the earth. Isles - The countries remote from Judea, shall gladly receive his doctrine.
He — This description of God's infinite power, is seasonably added, to give them assurance of the certain accomplishment of his promises.

Called thee — To declare my righteousness, or faithfulness. With-hold - Will give thee counsel and strength for the work. Give thee - To be the mediator in whom my covenant of grace is confirmed with mankind. The people - Of all people, not only of Jews but Gentiles. A light - To enlighten them with true and saving knowledge.

The Lord — Hebrew. Jehovah: who have all being in and of myself, and give being to all my creatures. The everlasting, and unchangeable, and omnipotent God, who therefore both can, and will fulfil all my promises.
I tell you — That when they come to pass, you may know that I am God, and that this is my work.

glossa.text:
*Behold my servant.* ((HIER.)) It is to be noted that the apostles are called Jacob, Israel, and the seed of Abraham, to whom afterward, as to servants and men, it is said: *Fear not, worm of Jacob,* etc. But Christ is called not the seed of Jacob or of Israel, but the servant.

*I have given my Spirit.* In the conception; whence: *The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee,* etc. ((Phil. II)). And it shone forth in the baptism, when the Spirit in the likeness of a dove rested upon him ((Luc. I)).

*Smoking flax.* The priesthood now almost extinguished; and of flax is the priestly vestment made.

*He shall bring forth judgment.* He shall judge, namely, not fearing the Scribes and the Pharisees.

*He shall not be sad.* ((ID.)) This Matthew did not set down; or else the words between the one *judgment* and the other were taken away by a copyist's error. And the sense is: he shall preserve at all times an evenness of countenance; which the philosophers falsely boast of Socrates, namely that he was neither sadder nor gladder than his wont.

*Judgment in the earth.* Whence: *For judgment I came into this world, that they who do not see may see,* etc. ((Joan. IX)).
*Justice.* It was just that he who was despised by the Jews should pass over through the apostles to the Gentiles.
*The bound.* With the cords of sins: in the Gospel, the Lord loosed him whom Satan had bound.
*To another.* The Son and the Holy Spirit is not another than the Father in the Godhead, and therefore has the same glory and the same praise.

*I will make known to you.* That you may know that I am the Lord, and there is none other beside me: and that you who behold the former things fulfilled may believe the things to come which I promise.

notes.text: Thy mercy — Mine enemies are cruel and perfidious, but thou art infinite in mercy, and faithfulness. Heavens - Is infinite and incomprehensible. Faithfulness - The truth both of thy threatenings against thine enemies, and of thy promises made to good men. The clouds - Is far above our reach, greater and higher than we can apprehend.

Mountains — Stedfast and unmoveable: eminent and conspicuous to all men. Judgments - The executions of thy counsels. Deep - Unsearchable, as the ocean. Man - The worst of men; yea, the brute-beasts have experience of thy care and kindness.
Loving-kindness — Though all thine attributes be excellent, yet, above all, thy mercy is most excellent, or precious and amiable.

Satisfied — Who trust in thee, as he now said. Fatness - With those delightful provisions, which thou hast prepared for them in heaven. The river - Which denotes both their plenty, and their perpetuity.

Life — It is in God as in a fountain, and from him is derived to us. But - Of that glorious and blessed, and endless life, which alone is worthy of the name. Light - In the light of thy glorious presence, which shall be fully manifested, when we see thee face to face. Light - Joy and comfort, and happiness: the word light is elegantly repeated in another signification; in the former clause it is light discovering, in this light, discovered or enjoyed.
The foot — Of my proud and insolent enemies. Come - So as to overthrow me.

glossa.text:
*O Lord, in heaven.* ((Cass.)) Good things are from God through mercy. As if he should say: Evils are from man, but goods from mercy. O Lord, in those who are *heaven,* that is, who know hidden things, is thy mercy: and that they themselves are *clouds,* is from thee. ((AUG.)) Or *in heaven,* that is, mercy, etc., *as far as* but announces by sending forth his truth.

*Even to the clouds.* That is, the preachers, through whom God thunders in announcing, flashes in miracles, rains in teachings. Who are also mountains, whom the sun first clothes with light, which afterward, from them and yet not by them, descends to the lowest of the valleys: for they are ministers of teaching, but God enlightens.

*Thy judgments.* ((AUG.)) That thou hast mercy on these, and blindest those; they are utterly searchable to none: yet thou savest both, these bodily only, those spiritually as well, wherein is great mercy.
*Men,* etc. He shows that temporal things also are from God.

*They shall be inebriated.* ((ID.)) The thing cannot be expressed, but by this likeness he intimates that, being full, they lose their mind, so that they no longer recognize their own fathers, sons, and other friends. Or, then they are drunk in reality, who now hope. *With the torrent.* As if: There shall be a rush of grace and mercy to inebriate them. ((ID.)) *With the torrent.* Not that the beatitude should be passing, but plentiful. Or, thy will breaks all obstacles in man. Or, the wisdom of Christ is a torrent, because it is sudden and swift.

*For with thee is the fountain of life.* ((CAS.)) *With thee,* O Christ, *is the fountain,* that is, the beginning of every good; and *in thy light,* because through his preaching we see the light of the Father and of the Holy Spirit, and therefore *hold forth,* that in this world one may go more safely.

notes.text: An high priest of good things to come — Described, ver. 15. Entered through a greater, that is, a more noble, and perfect tabernacle - Namely, his own body. Not of this creation - Not framed by man, as that tabernacle was.
The holy place — Heaven. For us - All that believe.

If the ashes of an heifer — Consumed by fire as a sin-offering, being sprinkled on them who were legally unclean. Purified the flesh - Removed that legal uncleanness, and re-admitted them to the temple and the congregation. Num. xix, 17, 18, 19.

How much more shall the blood of Christ. — The merit of all his sufferings. Who through the eternal Spirit - The work of redemption being the work of the whole Trinity. Neither is the Second Person alone concerned even in the amazing condescension that was needful to complete it. The Father delivers up the kingdom to the Son; and the Holy Ghost becomes the gift of the Messiah, being, as it were, sent according to his good pleasure. Offered himself - Infinitely more precious than any created victim, and that without spot to God. Purge our conscience - Our inmost soul. From dead works - From all the inward and outward works of the devil, which spring from spiritual death in the soul, and lead to death everlasting. To serve the living God - In the life of faith, in perfect love and spotless holiness.

And for this end he is the Mediator of a new covenant, that they who are called — To the engagements and benefits thereof. Might receive the eternal inheritance promised to Abraham: not by means of legal sacrifices, but of his meritorious death. For the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant - That is, for the redemption of transgressors from the guilt and punishment of those sins which were committed in the time of the old covenant. The article of his death properly divides the old covenant from the new.

glossa.text: *By a greater.* Christ entered the tabernacle, that is, heaven. By the name of the sign, that is, of the tabernacle, the Apostle designates the thing signified, that is, heaven, which is well called, *by a greater,* because it holds more than that earthly one, and *more perfect,* because there is perfect blessedness.
*Into the holies.* He expounds what he had said: *A tabernacle not made with hands, the holy of holies,* that is, heavenly things.

*For if the blood.* That through Christ there could be redemption, he proves from the lesser, because through those things of the law there was made a bodily cleansing. *Of goats.* The goat signifies Christ, through the likeness of the flesh of sin. Christ is called a bull, because with the horns of the two Testaments he tosses his enemies. *Unto the cleansing of the flesh,* that is, that the flesh might be cleansed on account of the precept of the law; but in Christ is perfection.

*He offered himself.* Christ, the mediator between God and men, is the giver of the New Testament: as high priest he is to us the giver of the new law. *Unspotted.* His blood is unspotted.

*From dead works;* that is, sins, which he who touches is defiled, as he who touched a dead body was defiled; nor does he enter into heaven, as neither did that man into the temple. *To the living.* Yet the death of Christ was necessary in the redemption not only of the Gentiles, but also of those transgressions which the law showed, it did not loose. So great was our sin, that we could not be saved unless the Only-begotten of God should die for us, who were debtors of death; but so he made us worthy of the Testament and of the promised inheritance, and thus the Testament was made firm.

*A death intervening.* Between the Old Testament and the New (in which not only the sacraments are divided, but the promises also) the distinction is the passion of Christ, in whose death it is certain that not earthly things are promised, but eternal. For in the death of the Only-begotten great things must needs be hoped for.

notes.text: Six days before the passover — Namely, on the Sabbath: that which was called by the Jews, "The Great Sabbath." This whole week was anciently termed "The great and holy week." Jesus came - From Ephraim, chap. xi, 54.

It seems Martha was a person of some figure, from the great respect which was paid to her and her sister, in visits and condolences on Lazarus' death, as well as from the costly ointment mentioned in the next verse. And probably it was at their house our Lord and his disciples lodged, when he returned from Jerusalem to Bethany, every evening of the last week of his life, upon which he was now entered.

Then Mary, taking a pound of ointment — There were two persons who poured ointment on Christ. One toward the beginning of his ministry, at or near Nain, Luke vii, 37, &c. The other six days before his last passover, at Bethany; the account of whom is given here, as well as by St. Matthew and Mark.
Against the day of my burial — Which now draws nigh.
The chief priests consulted, how to kill Lazarus also — Here is the plain reason why the other evangelists, who wrote while Lazarus was living, did not relate his story.

glossa.text: *He came into Bethania.* Therefore he came first to Bethania, that the raising of Lazarus might be handed down more deeply to the memory of all, and that the Jews might be confounded as inexcusable, plotting the death of so great a raiser of the dead.

*Mary therefore.* Precious ointment is made of nard, chiefly of the spikes; but here it is called pistic from the place whence it came. And it is interpreted "faithful," not corrupted by any other admixture. *Then said one.* Judas, although evil, is nevertheless numbered among the apostles, that we may be taught to bear with the evil, lest we divide the body of Christ, and that the evil do not harm the good.

*Not because,* etc. As far as his own intention went, it did not pertain to him concerning the needy, because he did not care for them; not because it had been committed to him to dispense to the poor.

*Having the purse,* etc. He to whom the angels minister has purses for the expenses of the poor, condescending to the weak.

*Let her alone.* He knows the thief, but does not betray him, teaching us to bear with the evil. He commends so great a service of Mary, showing that he was to die and to be anointed with spices for burial. Therefore to Mary, to whom it was not permitted to anoint him dead, it was given to bestow the office of a funeral upon him living; whence according to Mark it is said that what she had, that is, what she could, this she did, *she is come beforehand to anoint my body for the burial.*

*But me you have not always.* By bodily presence. Or you shall not have me, thou Judas and those who are of this sort, because if the evil now communicate in the sacraments, yet afterwards they do not have the Lord as the good do.

*And they came.* Curiosity brought these, not charity. We on the contrary, if we know that Jesus has found the house of an obedient soul in which to dwell, let us come thither by contemplation, not only for the sake of the man whom we see raised in the soul, but that we may imitate the good life, and through this come to the vision of Jesus.
*They thought.* Because they could not hide or deny the miracle, they foolishly wish to kill him, as though he who raised the dead man could not raise the slain.

echoes.text: Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, ‘Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.’
echoes.note: Moses' words at Sinai, inaugurating the first covenant in blood. Hebrews quotes them to make blood the necessary seal of any covenant — and so to read Christ's death as the blood that ratifies the new one: ‘apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.’

echoes.text: Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar. He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people, and they said, “All that Yahweh has spoken will we do, and be obedient.” Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.”
echoes.note: Beyond the quoted clause (v. 8), the whole narrative frame of vv. 19–20 — Moses reading ‘every commandment to all the people,’ then sprinkling — retells Exod 24:6–8. Hebrews adds details (water, scarlet wool, hyssop, sprinkling the book) not in Exod 24, conflating it with the purification rites (Num 19; Lev 14): high recurrence of the sprinkling motif drives the link.

echoes.text: “A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up outside of the camp in a clean place; and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for use in water for cleansing impurity. It is a sin offering.
echoes.note: ‘The ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled’ (v. 13) names the red-heifer rite of Num 19:9. Strong verbal volume (‘ashes of the heifer… cleansing impurity’) and exact thematic coherence: an outward cleansing ‘of the flesh’ that Hebrews contrasts with the inward cleansing of conscience by Christ's blood.

echoes.text: “For the unclean, they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the sin offering; and running water shall be poured into a vessel. A clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, on the persons who were there...
echoes.note: The mechanics of v. 13 (ashes + water sprinkled on the defiled) and the ‘water… and hyssop’ of vv. 19–21 echo Num 19:17–18, where hyssop dips the ash-water and sprinkles ‘the tent, all the vessels, the persons.’ Hebrews' phrase ‘sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels’ tracks this list closely — recurrence of sprinkling vocabulary.

echoes.text: The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the middle of the burning of the heifer.
echoes.note: ‘With water and scarlet wool and hyssop’ (v. 19) imports the ‘hyssop and scarlet’ of the heifer rite (Num 19:6) into the retelling of the Sinai covenant-cutting, which had neither. The conflation shows Hebrews reading all the blood-rites as one figural system; verbal contact on ‘scarlet… hyssop’ is the tell.
echoes.altSource: Leviticus 14:4–6 (scarlet and hyssop in the cleansing of the leper)

echoes.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.
echoes.note: ‘Apart from shedding of blood there is no remission’ (v. 22) crystallizes the principle of Lev 17:11 — blood makes atonement because the life is in it. No verbatim quotation, but high thematic coherence: this is the axiom on which the whole sacrificial argument of vv. 11–22 rests.

echoes.text: “Aaron shall come into the sanctuary with a young bull for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.
echoes.note: ‘The blood of goats and calves’ / ‘goats and bulls’ (vv. 12–13, 19) generalizes the Day-of-Atonement victims (bull and goat, Lev 16:3, 5–15). Faint and diffuse — Hebrews blends Day-of-Atonement animals with covenant-inauguration animals (Exod 24) — so verbal volume is low and the source is one strand among several.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: For the poor will never cease out of the land. Therefore I command you to surely open your hand to your brother, to your needy, and to your poor, in your land.
echoes.note: Jesus' 'you always have the poor with you' directly invokes Deut 15:11, 'the poor will never cease out of the land,' the Torah charge that grounds open-handed giving. High Volume by near-quotation and clear Availability; the allusion turns the verse's perpetual-poverty clause to relativize almsgiving against the unrepeatable burial of Messiah.

echoes.text: While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
echoes.note: Mary's pure nard whose fragrance fills the house echoes the Song's 'while the king was on his couch, my nard gave forth its fragrance.' The shared lexeme nardos (LXX) plus the banquet-couch setting and the diffusing scent give real Volume and Coherence; John frames the anointing of the messianic 'king' (the next pericope's title) in the idiom of the Bride's love-gift.

echoes.text: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits: henna with spikenard plants, spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,
echoes.note: The catalogue of spices 'nard and saffron... with all chief spices' supplies the only other biblical concentration of nard as a costly love-perfume, reinforcing the Songs register behind Mary's extravagant anointing. Low confidence: thematic resonance without verbal anchor beyond the shared spice.

echoes.text: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brothers: and the Spirit of Yahweh came mightily on David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
echoes.note: Anointing with oil is the act that makes a king/Messiah (christos); Mary's anointing of Jesus figurally enacts the royal-messianic identity the crowd will acclaim in v.13. Faint and contested, since John explicitly redirects the act toward burial rather than coronation.

echoes.text: They buried him in his own tombs, which he had dug out for himself in the city of David, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odors and various kinds of spices prepared by the perfumers’ art: and they made a very great burning for him.
echoes.note: Burial anointing with spices for a king (Asa) provides OT precedent for Jesus' reading of the nard as 'for the day of my burial.' Faint; the practice is generic enough that the link rests on theme rather than verbal contact.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The lamp is lit against the gathering dark.
In your light we see light.
Mary pours the nard; the house breathes its fragrance.
She has kept it for the day of his burial.
A bruised reed he will not break.
Come, let us worship the servant of the Lord.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The fragrance of Mary's nard still hangs in the room, costly and poured out, kept for the day of his burial.
The hour has come.
He will not break the bruised reed or quench the dimly burning wick; gently he leads the servant's way.
The hour has come.
With you is the fountain of life, and in your light we see light, even as the shadow lengthens toward the cross.
The hour has come.
So come near while the lamp still burns; the plot is laid, the road is set. Come, let us worship.
The hour has come. Amen.
